worksheet.title: Run It Top to Bottom
worksheet.subtitle: Blocks run in order, from the top down
worksheet.learning_goal: I can tell the order the blocks in a stack run.

parts.title: Top to bottom
parts.text: Bit runs a stack from the TOP block down. The top block runs first. Then the next block. Then the next — one block at a time, all the way to the bottom.

parts.title: Bit's stack
parts.note: Bit runs the top ⚑ block first, then works down: ➡, then ⬆, then ⬅ at the bottom.

parts.title: Runs first
parts.prompt: Circle the block Bit runs FIRST. Remember: Bit always starts at the top.

parts.title: Number the order
parts.prompt: Bit runs the stack from top to bottom. Write 1, 2, 3, 4 on the blocks above to show the order Bit runs them. The top ⚑ block is 1.

parts.title: You try
parts.prompt: Look at the new stack. Circle the block Bit runs LAST (the bottom one). Then write 1, 2, 3 on the blocks to show the run order.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: A program runs in order, from the top down, one block at a time. The order of the blocks is the algorithm — change the order and Bit does something different.

teacher_guide.eyebrow: Teacher Guide · Kindergarten · Intro Block Coding
teacher_guide.title: Run It Top to Bottom
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key
teacher_guide.footer_topic: 2. Run It Top to Bottom — Teacher Guide

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children learn that a block program runs from the top block down, one block at a time, and that where a block sits decides when it runs. The order of the blocks IS the plan. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper, a pencil, and a crayon. You read each prompt aloud. Optional: paper blocks (a green flag block + arrow blocks) to stack by hand, or floor boxes the child can walk.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Point to each block top to bottom and count: "first, next, next, last."
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — Bit runs the top GO block first.
3. Let them try. Children number the run order (Ex 2), then mark the last block and number the order (Ex 3).

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — Bit runs the top GO block first. Exercise 2 — order down the stack: GO = 1, right = 2, up = 3, left = 4.
Exercise 3 — the last block is the bottom right arrow; order down the second stack: GO = 1, left = 2, right = 3.

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for: numbering blocks bottom-up. The top block is always 1.
Make it easier: point to each block in order while the child writes the number.
Make it harder: ask which block runs third in a longer stack.
Make it active: children stand in a stack and sit down one at a time, top first.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children determine and describe the order in which a set of instructions is carried out.
In plain terms: the blocks run from the top down, one at a time — the order is the plan.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child circles, numbers, or draws an arrow.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child numbers the blocks top to bottom and names the first and last block.
